title: Utah immigration attorney says vehicle stops by ICE are 'one of the most used tools'
text:
President Donald Trump says Immigration and Customs Enforcement should continue using traffic stops as part of its immigration enforcement strategy, appearing t
FILE - In this July 8, 2019, file photo, a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer looks on during an operation in Escondido, Calif.
In a Truth Social post Wednesday, Trump praised ICE officers and called traffic stops one of the agency's "most important and effective" crime-fighting tools, saying officers should return to using the tactic while being "judicious, fair and smart.
" The post came after multiple national news organizations reported DHS had directed ICE officers to suspend most vehicle stops following fatal encounters in Maine and Texas while the incidents were reviewed. Hours after Trump's post, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the administration remained committed to arresting and deporting people in the country illegally, signaling the administration intended to continue aggressive immigration enforcement. Utah immigration attorney Carlos Trujillo said vehicle stops by ICE agents happen frequently.
Over the past year, several high-profile ICE traffic stops have involved people with ties to Utah, including a West Valley City operation that ended withTrujillo said if vehicle stops remain a cornerstone of immigration enforcement, the federal government should provide greater transparency and accountability.
"If this really is a key way of doing enforcement, where is the training? Where are the body cams?
" he said. "It is creating the uncertainty and fear that we have lived as a community for the last year and a half. We don't even understand anymore what is legal," Trujillo said. For people who are stopped by ICE, Trujillo said his advice is to remain calm, comply with officers' commands, and avoid escalating the encounter.
